newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas little changed ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas little changed ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices were mostly steady Friday ahead of the weekend, as storage buying in the producing region helped to support prices, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices for the most part held in the low-to-mid $1.80s per mmBtu, with Henry Hub mostly quoted at $1.85-1.87.

In south Texas, prices were steady to higher in the low-to-mid $1.80s, as storage buying continued in Texas and Oklahoma and traders waited for a nuclear unit in south Texas to return to the electricity grid.

Houston Lighting and Power's 1,250 megawatt South Texas 2 nuclear unit, which tripped off line Wednesday afternoon, was in startup mode early Friday morning and expected to be back on line sometime today.

On the East Coast, New York city-gate prices were about one to two cents lower in the low-$2.20s as seasonable temperatures were forecast for the region Saturday. A brief cold spell on Sunday and Monday is expected to be replaced with warmer weather Tuesday.
Sources said demand during brief cold spell would most likely be met by using the plentiful storage supplies.
In the Southwest, where temperatures are expected to cool off slightly early next week but remain above normal, prices at the southern California border edged up one cent to the low-to-mid $1.80s.
Meanwhile, Permian basin prices were little changed in the high-$1.60s.
Edison International reported earlier today that the 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California would likely restart next Wednesday.
In the Midcontinent, prices were little changed again at $1.73-1.76, with Demarcation quoted mostly in the mid-$1.70s.
Early April 1 differentials were about 15-17 cents under the screen, traders said.

Temperatures throughout the Midwest are forecast to climb to much above-normal levels Friday but then settle to near-normal by the weekend. Another warm front is expected to arrive Monday followed quickly by more cooler weather Tuesday.
